clue.text: Fussy cat pined terribly

indicators.note: terribly suggests the letters of cat and pined are badly jumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: A finicky cat is pining away badly.
explanation.definitionFit: A pedant is someone overly concerned with small details, so the adjective means nit-picking.

clue.text: Part of skin daughter concentrated on

parts.note: a pore is a tiny opening in the skin

explanation.surface: A dermatology student studied a patch of skin while a daughter looked on.
explanation.definitionFit: To pore over something is to study it intently, giving close attention.

clue.text: Notice way of speaking becomes a bad habit

parts.note: an ad is a notice in a newspaper
diction is a person's manner of enunciation

explanation.surface: Someone's affected speech has become an annoying tic.
explanation.definitionFit: A compulsive dependency on a substance or activity is commonly called a harmful habit.

clue.text: Eject those attending

explanation.definitionFit: To turn out is to throw someone out; a turnout is the number of people who come to an event.

clue.text: Rumours from Peking of changes in party message?

explanation.walkthrough: The second sense refers to the parlour game in which a message whispered from player to player comes out changed at the end; Peking is the old name for Beijing.
explanation.definitionFit: Read literally, gossip from China's capital; the party game where a murmured phrase passed round a circle gets garbled.

clue.text: European accepting Arab's word of honour

indicators.note: accepting means the European takes the other piece inside himself

parts.note: a Pole is a European from Poland
AR is an abbreviation for Arab or Arabic

explanation.surface: A man from Europe trusts the promise given by an Arab.
explanation.definitionFit: Parole originally meant a prisoner's solemn promise, a pledge given on one's honour.

clue.text: Refuelling operation — mine's best

parts.note: a pit is a coal mine, so mine's gives pits
top means best, as in top marks

explanation.surface: A boast that one's own colliery runs the finest fuel service.
explanation.definitionFit: In motor racing a car pulls in briefly mid-race for fuel and tyres; that halt is this.

clue.text: Bloke is building a monument

indicators.note: building suggests the letters of bloke and is are put together into a new structure

explanation.surface: A man is constructing a memorial.
explanation.definitionFit: A tall tapering four-sided stone pillar, such as Cleopatra's Needle, is a classic memorial.

clue.text: Meditates to reorganise thought

indicators.note: to reorganise asks for the letters of meditates to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone sits in contemplation in order to put their mind in order.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe a judgement reached roughly in the mind, as in a guessed figure.

clue.text: Book lecturer

explanation.walkthrough: In British universities a Reader is an academic rank above senior lecturer and below professor.
explanation.definitionFit: A primer for learning to read is called this; it is also a senior university teaching rank in Britain, just below professor.

clue.text: Profit from curiosity

explanation.definitionFit: Money earned on a loan or deposit is this, and so is the feeling of wanting to know more.

clue.text: Reveal girl's near

parts.note: Di is a short girl's name, so girl's gives Di's
close means near

explanation.surface: Announcing that a young woman is nearby.
explanation.definitionFit: To make known something previously secret is to divulge or uncover it.

clue.text: Boredom of Latin hymn we listen to

indicators.note: we listen to says the hymn's name is heard rather than seen, so it sounds like another word

parts.note: the Te Deum is a Latin hymn of praise

explanation.surface: Complaining about the dullness of having to sit through a Latin hymn.
explanation.definitionFit: Tedium is a state of weariness from monotony, the same feeling as ennui.

clue.text: Top social classes are wicked with the drink

parts.note: in British market research A and B are the highest social grades
to sin is to be wicked, the plural verb matching are
taken as written

explanation.surface: The upper classes are depraved, along with their tipple.
explanation.walkthrough: AB refers to the British social grading system, where A and B are the top classes.
explanation.definitionFit: A green aniseed-flavoured spirit flavoured with wormwood is a strong alcoholic beverage.

clue.text: Exercises in Wigan and Oldham, for example

explanation.walkthrough: Wigan and Oldham are towns in north-west England whose football clubs are both named Athletic, hence the plural.
explanation.definitionFit: Track and field sports are physical exertions; Wigan Athletic and Oldham Athletic are English football clubs.

clue.text: Ship — worth a lot?

explanation.walkthrough: In British slang a packet means a large sum of money.
explanation.definitionFit: A packet boat carried mail on a regular route; to cost a packet is British slang for being expensive.

clue.text: Line of children can be a vicious wild thing

explanation.walkthrough: A two-by-two file of schoolchildren is called a crocodile in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Schoolchildren walking in pairs in a column form this; it is also a large toothed reptile.

clue.text: For this church book, Henry exchanged many pounds

parts.note: H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance

indicators.note: exchanged signals that the letters of many are swapped around into a new order

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for pounds, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: Henry swapped a large sum of money for a hymn book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exchanged' turns MANY into YMNA, which sits between H and L.
explanation.definitionFit: A collection of sacred songs for congregational singing is a book used in services.

clue.text: Third note wrong — amend it

indicators.note: wrong suggests the letters of amend and it are in the wrong order and must be rearranged

explanation.surface: A musician spots a mistaken third note and is told to fix it.
explanation.definitionFit: In music theory the third degree of a diatonic scale has this name.

clue.text: Left to set light to the coal

parts.note: to ignite is to set light to something

explanation.surface: Someone was left to get the coal fire going.
explanation.definitionFit: A soft brownish fuel, also called brown coal, is a low-grade type of this.

clue.text: Revered college had debts

parts.note: a hall is a college or residence at a university
owed means had debts

explanation.surface: A respected university college was actually in debt.
explanation.definitionFit: Hallowed means held sacred, honoured and greatly respected.

clue.text: Cordelia is only a girl having an affair

indicators.note: having means the words Cordelia is only contain the answer within them

explanation.surface: Cordelia is just a young woman caught up in a romance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a girl' is surface padding; the answer runs through 'Cordelia is only'.
explanation.definitionFit: A secret romantic relationship is a liaison, another term for an amour.

clue.text: Transmitting not the start, but the finish

indicators.note: not the start means the first letter of the word for transmitting is dropped

parts.note: sending means transmitting

explanation.surface: A broadcaster insists it was the conclusion, not the opening, being aired.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not the start' removes the S from SENDING.
explanation.definitionFit: The close or conclusion of a story or event is how it ends.

clue.text: On a ship, going past Kent coast

indicators.note: going past means the ship piece follows on after the county piece

parts.note: Kent is a county in south-east England, so it is indicated by SE
aboard means on a ship

explanation.surface: Passengers on a vessel sail by the shores of Kent.
explanation.walkthrough: Kent is a county in the south-east of England, hence SE.
explanation.definitionFit: The land along the edge of the sea is the shoreline.

clue.text: Avoid American city

explanation.definitionFit: To evade something is to dodge it; Dodge City is a town in Kansas famous from the Wild West.

clue.text: In the fourth part of the play hand is idle

parts.note: taken as written

parts.words: the fourth part of the play
parts.note: the fourth division of a play is Act IV
E for East, one of the four hands at bridge

explanation.surface: A stagehand does nothing during the fourth act of a play.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge the four players, or hands, are North, South, East and West, so a hand can be E.
explanation.definitionFit: Being idle means not working or doing anything, i.e. not busy.

clue.text: Son felt sick as he left harbour

parts.note: ailed means felt ill

explanation.surface: A boy felt seasick as his ship departed port.
explanation.definitionFit: A vessel that set out to sea from port departed by this means.

clue.text: Tries a crazy sort of humour

indicators.note: crazy suggests the letters of tries and a are mixed up wildly

explanation.surface: Someone attempts a zany style of comedy.
explanation.definitionFit: Ridicule or irony used to mock folly is a form of comic writing.

clue.text: A few words from the judge

explanation.definitionFit: A grammatical unit of words is one sense; the punishment a court pronounces on a convicted person is the other.
